store_data.about_the_game:
〇 Genre

2D Strategy Board Game

〇 Game Mechanics

Two players each select six units (pieces) and operate them on a 6x6 board.

This game does not have a clear turn system; the command order of units is determined by their stats.

The command order can be changed through player actions during the game.

Units level up over time, strengthening their stats and allowing them to select commands such as attack and strengthen.

Each unit has its own stats, arts (attack techniques, support techniques), and skills, so choose units that match your strategy and tactics.

When a unit reaches a certain level, it can evolve into a new unit that can significantly change the course of the battle, and its stats will be greatly enhanced.

Use arts (attack techniques) to attack your opponent's units when selecting commands. When a unit's durability reaches 0, it is destroyed.

Destroying a certain number of your opponent's units wins the game.

〇 Game Modes

MAGISTAL implements Free Duel Mode and Story Mode.

Free Duel Mode allows you to select your favorite units and battle against other players (Player 1 vs. Player 2).

Player 2 can be designated as a CPU, allowing Player 1 to battle alone.

Story Mode allows you to experience the world of MAGISTAL in an episodic format.

You progress through the story by repeatedly selecting episodes, watching character conversations, and engaging in battles.

Clearing certain episodes unlocks more units.

〇Story

As the eldest son of one of the four great noble families ruling the kingdom, you will win territorial disputes against other nobles through duels.

There is an absolute rule that all disputes between nobles must be resolved through duels, and the winner receives the conditions presented by the loser; there is no resistance to this coercive force.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Hidden Camp is an online multiplayer social deduction survival game for 9 players, set in a mysterious forest camp where trust is fragile and every decision matters.

At first, everyone appears to be part of the same group. Players gather around the camp, complete tasks, explore the environment, and try to survive each round. But among them, hidden traitors are waiting for the right moment to create chaos.

The campers must work together, complete their objectives, and identify who cannot be trusted. The traitors must stay hidden, mislead the group, and eliminate the campers before they are exposed.

Every round is shaped by suspicion, strategy, timing, and betrayal.

SOCIAL DEDUCTION IN A MYSTERIOUS CAMP

No one knows who they can fully trust. A helpful player may be protecting the group, or secretly guiding everyone toward danger.

Observe player behavior, question suspicious actions, and make careful decisions before it is too late.

COMPLETE TASKS AND SURVIVE

Campers can progress by completing tasks around the map. Teamwork is important, but moving alone can be dangerous.

Every completed task brings the campers closer to victory, while every mistake gives the traitors more control over the round.

HIDDEN TRAITORS

Traitors must blend in with the group, avoid suspicion, and strike when the moment is right.

Use deception, movement, and timing to confuse the campers and survive long enough to win.

CAMP LEADER SYSTEM

Each round includes a Camp Leader who gains special responsibility during the match. The leader can influence the flow of the game and make important decisions that may change the outcome of the round.

But power does not always mean safety.

PROXIMITY VOICE CHAT

Communication plays a key role in The Hidden Camp. Players can talk through proximity voice chat, making conversations feel more natural and tense.

Who you hear, what you say, and when you speak can all affect whether others trust you.

KEY FEATURES

  • Online multiplayer matches for 9 players

  • Social deduction gameplay with hidden traitors

  • Task-based survival objectives

  • Camp Leader role with special gameplay impact

  • Proximity voice chat

  • Suspicion, betrayal, and teamwork in every round

  • Stylized 3D characters and a mysterious forest camp atmosphere

TRUST NO ONE

In The Hidden Camp, survival is not only about completing tasks.

It is about reading people, hiding your intentions, making the right accusations, and surviving long enough to reveal the truth.

Work together. Stay alert. Find the traitors. Survive the camp.

store_data.about_the_game:
🚂 Doomsday Train: A Mobile Haven on Rails

When the world collapses in the apocalypse and cities lie in ruins, the order of civilization has long ceased to exist. Only the rusted railway tracks still stretch across the barren wasteland, carrying humanity’s last hope. You will take command of an end-of-the-world train, leading a group of survivors to fight for survival from your mobile stronghold.

🔧 Refit Your Train to Build a Mobile Home

Unlike traditional colony survival games, you don’t need to build permanent houses or walls — every carriage of your train is your workshop, storage, medical bay, and living quarters.

  • Rearrange carriage layouts, build facilities, and construct an efficient survival network in limited space.

  • Maintain the train engine, reinforce armor, and keep it moving forward through the dangers of the wasteland.

  • Assign jobs and roles to survivors, ensuring every member of the team contributes to your survival.

☀️ Dynamic Extreme Weather Tests Your Strategy

On the wasteland, danger never follows a pattern:

  • Sandstorms wear down train parts, while radiation clouds force you to seal carriages immediately.

  • Blizzards freeze the tracks, and sweltering heat spoils food — every weather condition requires advance preparation.

  • Threats like zombie hordes and raiders can breach your defenses at any time.

🧠 Deep Survival Management and Tough Choices

Survival is more than just gathering resources:

  • Manage food, water, and fuel carefully to travel farther in the resource-scarce wasteland.

  • Care for survivors’ health, moods, and needs — illness and depression can tear the team apart.

  • Face moral dilemmas: accept strangers or conserve supplies? Risk scavenging or play it safe? Your decisions shape everyone’s fate.

🎮 Immersive Side-Scrolling Perspective

Featuring a 2.5D side view , you’ll witness the struggles of life inside the carriages up close, feeling the tension and despair of the end of the world.

🔧 Refit Your Train to Build a Mobile Home

Unlike traditional colony survival games, you don’t need to build permanent houses or walls — every carriage of your train is your workshop, storage, medical bay, and living quarters.

  • Rearrange carriage layouts, build facilities, and construct an efficient survival network in limited space.

  • Maintain the train engine, reinforce armor, and keep it moving forward through the dangers of the wasteland.

  • Assign jobs and roles to survivors, ensuring every member of the team contributes to your survival.

On the wasteland, danger never follows a pattern:

  • Sandstorms wear down train parts, while radiation clouds force you to seal carriages immediately.

  • Blizzards freeze the tracks, and sweltering heat spoils food — every weather condition requires advance preparation.

  • Threats like zombie hordes and raiders can breach your defenses at any time.

🧠 Deep Survival Management and Tough Choices

Survival is more than just gathering resources:

  • Manage food, water, and fuel carefully to travel farther in the resource-scarce wasteland.

  • Care for survivors’ health, moods, and needs — illness and depression can tear the team apart.

  • Face moral dilemmas: accept strangers or conserve supplies? Risk scavenging or play it safe? Your decisions shape everyone’s fate.

🎮 Immersive Side-Scrolling Perspective

Featuring a 2.5D side view , you’ll witness the struggles of life inside the carriages up close, feeling the tension and despair of the end of the world.

store_data.about_the_game:
I originally developed this game for release under the holo Indie brand, but it was not approved by CCMC Corporation.

They said I could still release it independently, so here is the game.

Supports DLSS and FSR.

This game features Pekora and Vivi from hololive (and contains some references that only fans will understand).

Using either a baseball bat or a golf club, Pekora launches Vivi — who is inside a ball — downhill.

You can somewhat control the ball using the [W][A][S][D] keys.

But gravity can easily overpower your controls.

The ball has health points, and it takes more or less damage depending on the surface it is rolling over. For example, it takes less damage on sand and more damage on rocks.

When the ball’s HP reaches 0, it breaks open and Vivi flies out and rolls across the ground.

If this happens near some items, an event can happen. I.E. If you land near a chest, Pekora will open it and obtain a new item.

This detection range depends on the baseball bat or golf club equipped.

You can select the new bat or ball from the main menu (press Esc)

There is a menu that lists all missions, with filters to show or hide completed missions. The list is sorted by name.

Whenever you see a gate with a blinking yellow light, it means it is the first gate of a mission.

However, not all missions have a gate with a blinking yellow light. For example, in the bowling missions, you must knock down all the pins.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Stage

The main stage of this work is a space research vessel named "Xiange". Lost in space and out of contact with Earth, the vessel forms an unconventional "stormy mountain villa", making it an ideal setting for a honkaku mystery story...

Story Background

The protagonist, Chen Chou, is invited by a friend to take part in a strange experiment. During the experiment, Chen Chou enters a bizarre container. When he regains consciousness, he finds himself aboard a space research vessel. Stranger still, the crew members—whom Chen Chou has never met—all claim to know him. Could it be that he has traveled to a parallel world? And soon after, murders begin to occur one after another...

A reasoning experience that emphasizes player agency

In typical mystery games, the deduction segments often follow a fixed process: players are only asked to reason at key moments, spending most of their time watching characters discuss rather than deducing on their own. This makes it hard to experience the authentic honkaku mystery thrill of starting from scratch and unraveling the truth step by step.

The deduction system of Parallel Lines Intersection Murder Case aims to stimulate players’ initiative in independent reasoning. The reasoning process is actively controlled by the player—which line of thought or clue to start with is decided by the player, rather than following a fixed in-game sequence.

Reasoning and story influenced by parallel worlds

Depending on whether the player uses parallel-world-related clues during deduction, the reasoning will diverge significantly, potentially leading to completely different murders and methods. At the same time, it will also affect the subsequent direction of the story.

4772190.name: Master of the Ages: Foundations of History

store_data.about_the_game:
Master of the Ages is a historical 4X strategy game focused on the mechanics of empire building. From the Ancient world to the Modern era, you direct the macro-strategy of your civilization across six eras of human history. The visual presentation favors clean, tidy graphics, making it easy to see what is actually happening across your empire at a glance.

CITIES THAT SPECIALIZE

Cities are differentiated through structural infrastructure choices, not just tile output. Starting in the Classical era, several key buildings come in mutually exclusive pairs: build the Market District for trade and growth, and the Artisan Quarter — better suited to cities sitting on hills and mining terrain — is permanently locked out. By the late game, most of your cities will have settled into distinct roles and flavors based on the infrastructure choices you committed to along the way.
  • A single currency & Urban Capacity. No gold, no influence, no parallel economies to juggle. Production Points are the empire's entire economy — upkeep, construction, and research all draw from the same pool. However, growth is strictly bounded by Urban Capacity; a city's population will stall until you commit production to infrastructure that physically expands its urban footprint.
  • Queue-driven production. Allocate Production Points to what you want built — buildings, armies, founding projects. Unspent PP converts to Research Points up to a per-city Scholarly Capacity (raised by Libraries, Universities, and similar). Beyond capacity the conversion drops off sharply, so idle production cannot be silently converted into unlimited research.
  • City Focus. Each city declares its purpose. Growth and Production focuses are available from the start; Military and Science focuses unlock through later civic technologies. An automated governor handles tile-by-tile improvement decisions according to the focus, leaving the bigger picture to you.
  • No settler units. There is no settler to micromanage. Mature cities project new ones through founding projects, with real constraints on distance, supply lines, and food provisioning from the parent city.

COMPOSITE ARMIES, REAL LOGISTICS

Combat is automatic and resolves over several rounds, with the option to retreat between rounds. Each round runs through structured phases — Air, Artillery, Ranged, Cavalry, Melee, Support — and your composite armies engage according to the unit classes they pool together. Type advantages, terrain modifiers, veterancy, and morale all factor into outcomes. Battles play out quickly but the results feel grounded — armies that take heavy damage break morale and rout, and sieges require actual siege weapons — you will not breach a fortified city with cavalry.

The strategic layer is what gets armies into a fight:
  • Supply networks with finite range, chained supply depots, and depot positions enemies can target to disrupt your campaign.
  • Movement types (Foot, Mounted, Wheeled, Tracked, Motorized) that interact with terrain and roads — mountain passes matter, river crossings matter, road infrastructure matters.
  • Zone of Control that turns terrain choke points into real tactical decisions without requiring you to micromanage individual units.
  • Naval and air domains with embarking constrained by your port infrastructure's transport capacity, escort mechanics, coastal bombardment, and submarine stealth. Fleets patrol open water to engage hostile ships and shield vulnerable, embarked armies from interception.
  • Unified urban defense — cities defend with walls, militia, and garrison together. Taking a fortified city means breaking through each layer in turn.

FIVE BRANCHES OF PROGRESS

Technology is structured across five parallel categories — Agriculture, Engineering, Science, Civics, and Military — so your civilization develops as a coherent society rather than a single line on a tree.
  • Boost any category to accelerate research where you most need it.
  • Era advancement requires meaningful breadth across all five categories. You cannot sprint through Ancient by ignoring everything but Military.
  • Cross-category prerequisites create genuine strategic chains across the tree.
Six eras span Ancient through Modern, with technologies grounded in their historical context.

COVERT POWER

Beyond open warfare, you run espionage networks that gather intelligence on rivals, steal technologies, and execute sabotage. Espionage uses a deterministic friction model rather than dice rolls — the outcome of an operation is legible from its inputs, and a rival hiding a tech lead behind closed borders is a problem you can solve with patience and infiltration rather than luck.

THREE PATHS TO VICTORY

The Modern Era drives the world toward a climax. As any nation closes in on a victory condition, a global Doomsday Clock appears — alerting all players to the impending threat. There are no quiet, behind-the-scenes finishes.

Military Victory — Full Spectrum Dominance
Achieve a global Combat Strength (CS) of at least 1.5× the combined total of all surviving rivals to trigger a 10-turn surrender countdown. No tedious, city-by-city mop-up required. However, because CS scales dynamically with current unit HP%, a global coalition can pause or reset your countdown by damaging your forces via artillery, airstrikes, or skirmishes.

Economic Victory — Mars Colonization
Construct both a Spaceport and a Fusion Reactor to unlock the continuous Launch Mars Payload project. Every Production Point allocated across these specialized industrial hubs converts directly into tonnage toward a one-million-ton threshold. To stop you, rival nations must physically bomb your spaceports or capture your launch cities.

Science Victory — AI Singularity
Construct specialized AI Research Labs across your empire and flood them with Research Points. The Doomsday Clock displays the exact turns remaining until the Singularity completes, painting an immediate target on your top science hubs for the rest of the world.

NUCLEAR WEAPONS

The Modern Era introduces nuclear options, permanently reshaping both the map and the user. A strike scorches a seven-hex radius into a lasting wasteland. Crucially, the aggressor accumulates stacking domestic instability — protests, unrest, and lost urban capacity — while retaliatory strikes carry no such domestic penalty. Striking first cripples your own empire; striking back does not.

A NOTE ON DESIGN PHILOSOPHY

Master of the Ages is built for players who value systemic depth and clear feedback. The map favors readability over visual density, and the mechanics reward long-term planning over mechanical busywork.
With a unified economy driven by a single currency and an automated tile-management system, players do not need to manage individual settler movements, route spies across hexes, or handle granular micromanagement. Time spent in menus is focused entirely on making high-level, strategic decisions about the macro-development of your civilization.

store_data.about_the_game:
Astral Dive is a fantasy pixel art RPG that pays homage to the great classics of the genre, reinventing exploration and combat with modern and dynamic mechanics.

Step into the shoes of Atlas, a young and promising mage, as you cross the threshold of astral portals, explore fascinating dimensions, and investigate the mysterious events that shook the academy of magic years ago. Will you uncover the truth and protect your world?

Unique and Strategic Turn-Based Combat

Forget typical turn-based battles. In Astral Dive, combat blends the tactical planning of classic JRPGs with an original system of stellar tiles (magic cards). Collect new spells during your journey, customize your deck, and create lethal synergies to defeat bizarre creatures and colossal bosses.

A Journey Beyond Astral Portals

Story-Driven Dark Fantasy RPG with Precision Turn-Based Combat

Requiem for Faith is a dark fantasy turn-based RPG built around precision combat, set in Varnath, a kingdom of seven cities standing at the edge of a breaking faith

Play as a Fallen Holy Knight

Once protected by holy vows and sacred light, the kingdom now trembles under war, fear, and secrets buried beneath the Cathedral. Lead Seraphine, Captain of the Holy Knights, through a realm where demons are not your only enemies, and where every truth comes at a cost

Master Parry, Dodge, and Ritual Timing

Battle is built around precision, not just power. Parry devastating attacks, dodge at the right moment, and master Ritual timing to unleash stronger ultimate skills. Every encounter asks you to read the enemy, control the rhythm of battle, and survive when brute force is not enough

Form Accords and Unlock Forbidden Power

Forge Accords with gods, demons, and forces beyond mortal understanding. Call upon them in battle, unlock powerful abilities, and decide what kind of power you are willing to accept in order to survive

Choices That Shape Your Faith

Your choices shape more than dialogue. The Faith system affects the story, rewards, character paths, and what you may become. Mercy, doubt, devotion, and defiance can all leave their mark on the world and the people who still believe in it

Explore a Kingdom Torn by War and Secrets

Explore ruined villages, haunted forests, sacred halls, hidden paths, and places where the line between holy and monstrous begins to fade. In Varnath, every city hides a wound, every oath has a price, and every enemy wears a different face

Key Features

  • Experience an estimated 40 - 50 hours of story-driven RPG content across 7 chapters, with main story progression, side quests, optional encounters, and secrets to uncover

  • Power may make you stronger, but timing is what makes you win. Parry, dodge, counter, and master the rhythm of precision-based turn-based combat

  • Make choices that shape the story, rewards, character paths, and what you become. Every decision carries weight

  • Forge Accords with gods, demons, and ancient powers, then call upon them to turn the tide of battle

  • Explore Varnath, a kingdom of seven cities torn between faith, war, demons, and human ambition

  • Witness cinematic character cut-ins, brutal battles, and unforgettable encounters against enemies both holy and monstrous

store_data.about_the_game:
SECTOR NULL

You are deep underground in a massive industrial research facility. A containment breach has let out something biological, fleshy, and extremely hostile.

Even worse: you’ve caught the virus. It’s slowly mutating inside your body, corrupting your vision, and eating away at your sanity.

Your only companion is VERA - a fully-voiced artificial intelligence guiding you through the dark. She overrides security gates and tells you what systems to fix to proceed. But as your infection gets worse and her instructions start sounding suspicious, you have to ask yourself: can you actually trust her?

FEATURES

Every Run is Different The sub-surface layout changes every time you play. You'll navigate through up to 250 procedurally generated rooms per run - ranging from reactor chambers and server hubs with blinking LED grids, to creaking metal walkways hanging over a bottomless void.

Fight the Infection, or Lose Your Mind The virus isn't just a status bar. As your corruption levels spike, your vision distorts and the environment begins to warp. Keep your head together, because reaching maximum corruption means losing your mind entirely. However, some alternate paths out of the facility might require you to embrace the rot.

Get Your Hands Dirty on the Terminals You can't just run to the exit. You’ll have to physically interact with industrial systems to escape. Replace blown server fuses, vent steam pressure valves, reboot corrupted memory cores, and drain pools of acid or radioactive waste to clear your path.

Conserve Your Energy, or Stay Silent Resources are scarce. Your flashlight battery is constantly draining. Sometimes, staying crouched in the shadows is your only way to survive the Crawlers, Watchers, and whatever else is stalking you from the abyss.

Permanent Upgrades Surviving runs and unlocking achievements gets you coins. Spend them in the shop to permanently upgrade your character for future attempts: buy the Glock, increase your run speed, make your flashlight batteries last longer, or boost your health and stamina.

15 Achievements, Multiple Endings How will you get out? Escaping normally is just one option. You can overload the nuclear reactor, isolate yourself in quarantine to save the surface, yield to VERA’s suspicious demands, or even manage a bizarre symbiosis with the creatures. Find all the endings and unlock the ultimate achievements.

Welcome to the wildest race to the top! Wild Climbers: Peak Panic is a hilarious, physics-driven multiplayer party game where speed, strategy, and a little bit of luck are your best friends.

The goal is simple: Reach the highest point in the forest before the timer hits zero. The execution? Pure chaos.

Key Features:

  • Online Multiplayer Mayhem: Jump into fast and frantic lobbies supporting 2 to 10 players. Play with your friends in private rooms or challenge climbers from around the world.

  • 3-Minute Madness: No time to waste! You only have 3 minutes to scale the environment, making every second and every jump count. Keep moving, or get left behind.

  • Dodge, Dash, and Survive: The climb isn't a walk in the park. Navigate through a variety of tricky obstacles, unpredictable traps, and handy boosters. One wrong step can send you tumbling all the way down!

  • Quirky Characters: Choose from a roster of funny and bizarre characters—from rattling skeletons to goofy zombies—and climb in style.

  • High Replayability: Fast rounds, unpredictable physics, and hilarious rivalries mean no two climbs are ever the same.

Do you have what it takes to survive the panic and conquer the peak? Jump in, avoid the traps, and leave your friends in the dust!

Road Ready VR is a virtual reality driving simulator designed to help beginner and anxious drivers practice real road scenarios in a safe, controlled environment.

Built around confidence, repetition, and realistic road awareness, Road Ready VR lets players experience common driving situations before facing them in real life. Practice city driving, parking, lane changes, intersections, highways, traffic lights, road signs, and road-test style scenarios from inside a first-person VR driving environment.

The PC VR version is currently in development and is being prepared for SteamVR.

• Practice driving in a safe virtual environment

• First-person VR cockpit experience

• City driving, parking, and highway-style scenarios

• Traffic lights, signs, intersections, and lane awareness

• Beginner-friendly lessons and road-test style practice

• Free roam driving areas

• Vehicle garage and customization systems

• Designed for confidence-building, practice, and learning

Road Ready VR is not a replacement for licensed driving instruction, official road tests, local traffic laws, or real-world supervised driving practice. Always follow your local traffic laws and official guidance.

store_data.about_the_game:
Roll. Hide your cup. Then lie through your teeth.

Bardo is a game of bluffing and nerve for up to 6 players, classic Liar's Dice with a cozy tavern soul and a chaotic twist.

How it works

Everyone rolls five dice in secret. Take turns raising the bid on how many of a face are on the whole table. Think they're lying? Call their bluff. Think they nailed it exactly? Call Spot On. Lose the round, lose a die. Last one with dice on the table wins.

Bluff with friends or strangers

Up to 6 players online. Host a private table for your friends, or drop into an open lobby and lie to whoever shows up.

The loser writes the rules

In Event mode, whoever loses the round picks a twist for the next one: only one face counts, every cup lifts for a single second, you can't peek at your own hand for more than two… Chaos, by popular demand.

Play solo, never alone

Not in the mood for people? Fill the table with AI rivals. 7 distinct personalities, some cautious, some reckless, some impossible to read. (Meet Rum, Ace, Raven… and the rest.

Make the table yours

Unlock 13 characters, from grizzled adventurers to outright oddballs, each earned through its own challenge, win with a single die, land five perfect Spot On calls, pull off a +10 raise. Then pick your victory pose and gloat in style

A warm place to lie

A hand-built medieval tavern, an original soundtrack, and the firelit, friendly menace of a good story about pirates and chancers. No grimdark, just good company and bad intentions.

Features

  • Up to 6 players online

  • Solo play vs. 7 AI rivals, each with a personality of their own

  • Two modes: Classic and chaotic Events

  • 13 unlockable characters with their own challenges, plus victory poses

  • Public lobbies & private tables

  • English, Spanish, Russian, Português (Brasil), 简体中文

store_data.about_the_game:
Levitar 3D

A high-gravity arcade lander. Thrust, tractor, and shoot your way through procedural alien worlds — collect every pod, harvest tech from the wrecks, and don't run out of fuel.

About This Game

Levitar 3D is a modern take on the gravity-bound lander — the lineage of Thrust, Lunar Lander, and Choplifter, rebuilt around a 3D arena, escalating gravity, and a salvage-loop economy.

You pilot a thrust-driven ship across procedurally built worlds. Every level hands you the same task: collect the pods, recover the cargo, and return to the landing pad. Stranded survivors don't tractor themselves home. Fuel runs out fast. And the planetary defenses — turrets, hover tanks, airborne drones, heat-seeking missiles, flying saucers — get nastier the deeper you push.

When an enemy dies it leaves a wreck. Wrecks drop tech. Tow them home with the tractor beam and you'll bolt new weapons and shields onto your ship for the runs ahead. Die and respawn — you keep your tech. Run out of lives and the run is over.

Each tier of difficulty cranks gravity heavier. By the time you reach the deep levels your ship is fighting to stay aloft, a single brush with the wrong wall means a crash, and one missile hit means instant death. Side missions pile on optional cargo — some of it volatile, ready to detonate on the slightest impact. Sealed loot vaults wait at every milestone, and a steady score keeps earning you fresh ships to throw at the climb.

Features

- Procedural arenas — every level is rebuilt fresh. Obstruction layouts, multi-story tube mazes, enemy spawns, side-mission cargo.

- Gravity ramp — difficulty isn't a number on a slider, it's the actual physics. Heavier worlds bend your flight envelope.

- Tech salvage loop — shoot, kill, tractor the wreck home. Weapons, shields, and beam tech stack across the run.

- Escalating enemy roster — turrets, hover tanks, hover defenders, heat-seeking missiles, flying saucers — each unlocked at a deeper tier.

- Tractor beam economy — drag pods, drag wrecks, siphon fuel from enemies mid-tow. A direct hit on the collector pays out points, fuel, and tech.

- Side missions — reactor cores, cryo pods, data vaults, beacon relays, plasma conduits. Each is tagged on-screen so you can spot it in the chaos, and some are too unstable to bump.

- Loot vaults — sealed chambers surface every tenth level. Tractor the roof off and claim the mystery weapon spinning inside.

- Navigation HUD — a top-screen minimap and a ring of directional arrows around your ship track every pod, enemy, mission target, and the collector. Tow cargo and a single arrow points you home.

- Briefing flythrough — every level opens with a camera sweep across the arena and a full readout: pods to collect, enemy breakdown, gravity tier, ship status, and installed tech.

- Earn extra ships — every 250,000 points buys another ship, and a big bonus payout can award several at once.

- Milestone restarts — game over isn't back to square one. Restart from any milestone you've reached — every tenth level unlocks as you climb.

- Replay any cleared level — re-roll a level for a higher score or different tech drops, with full inventory rollback.

- Run stats tallied — kills, accuracy, fuel consumed, perfect clears, time played — all logged at game over.

- Persistent progression — level number, tech, shields, and points save between sessions. Pick up where you left off.

Salvageable Weapons

Every hover tank and flying saucer you destroy has a chance to leave a weapon behind. Tractor the wreck back to the collector and the tech bolts onto your ship — switch between everything you've acquired with the mouse wheel. Weapon drops start at deeper levels; until then enemies drop defensive Shield Units to harden the hull for what's coming. Loot vaults are the other source — crack one open and the weapon inside is yours to tow home.

Projectile Weapons

- Plasma Repeater — Your starting sidearm. Rapid-fire green bolts. Reliable, cheap, never not useful.

- Ion Orb — Slow-flying spheres of charged ion that punch hard. Lead your targets.

- Phoenix Round — A burning round that ignites on impact and chews through hull plating.

- Inferno Burst — A heavier cousin of Phoenix. Bigger payload, bigger crater.

- Pulse Laser — Hitscan-fast green beam. Trades raw damage for instant delivery.

- Disruptor Bolt — Charged laser bolts that scramble enemy systems on contact.

- Photon Stinger — Tiny darts of focused light fired in dense bursts.

- Tesla Coil — Crackling arc of lightning that leaps between nearby targets.

- Acid Spitter — Lobs corrosive globules that eat through armor over time.

- Plasma Lance — Concentrated plasma jet — short range, devastating up close.

- Void Ripper — Tears a small rift in space at the impact point. Don't ask what's on the other side.

- Halo Disc — Spinning disc that arcs through the air and slices clean through hardened targets.

- Resonance Ring — Pulses outward in waves. Useful for crowded approaches.

- Seeker Missile — Compact homing missile. Locks on the nearest hostile and chases it down.

- Hunter Lance — A heavier guided spike. Slower than Seeker, but punches deeper.

- Concussion Wave — Releases a kinetic shockwave that knocks light units sideways.

- Crystal Burst — Shatter-shot of crystalline shrapnel — spreads on contact, hits multiple targets.

Beam Weapon

- Static Gun — Held-fire continuous beam. Anything its line touches dies instantly. Drains fuel as long as the trigger's down — every second you hold it is one less second in the air.

Ordnance

- Frag Bomb — Dropped charge. Detonates on impact, peppers the area with shrapnel.

- Heavy Munition — Oversized payload — larger blast radius, longer fuse. Be elsewhere when it goes off.

- Antimatter Charge — Subatomic warhead. The blast doesn't care about cover. Don't be in the radius.

store_data.about_the_game:
A relaxing fishing trip from the comfort of your desktop! Up Pole! is a desktop companion idler and pomodoro timer designed to add a little life to your computer time from the corner of your screen. Join Mr. Skip on a relaxing trip to scenic fishing spots, and drop a line in the water while you work or unwind!

  • Cast a line while you work to spice up your time on the computer, and unwind with a real-time fishing slow-burn experience

  • Add some life to your desktop  - keep your best catches in your own virtual living aquarium

  • Real-time, real fishin' - a dynamic day-to-night system is tied to your real system clock, affecting not just visuals but fish behaviors and activity levels!

  • No-stress lite progression - sell the fish you reel in for better tackle to aim for more exotic species! Are you a sharp enough angler to collect all the species in the game? 

  • Built-in pomodoro timer easily accessible to keep you sharp off while you're off the water!

-=-=--==-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-

Director's Note

When I was kid, about 6 or so, my grandpa started taking me on fishing trips with him in and around town. We'd wake up way before the crack of dawn and dig for night-crawlers in his yard, then drive for hours out to the middle of nowhere to find a spot all to ourselves. As the sun would peek over the treeline he'd show me how setup my line, bait my hook (I hated that part), and finally cast out as far as we could in the hopes of pulling in a big ol' bass - usually for lil E, it was more likely a "sunny", but every now and then I'd get lucky, reel my heart out, and pull a reel keeper out of the water. He was a mean cook, and we'd fry up whatever we caught that very day. He was a real outdoors-man, and although I didn't get to learn everything he wanted to teach me in the time we had together I'll always cherish what I did learn: what it means to respect and love nature, to stick with things even when they're hard (and even when the stupid hook keeps sticking in your stupid thumb), and that anything worth doing takes a little bit of time and whole lotta patience.

My brother/concept artist Seth and I kicked this idea around for a while, and now while we're releasing smaller projects to keep the lights on and gear-up for our bigger works it felt like a natural game to make. I built this one "jam"-style, and while I was working on the design I realized that I wouldn't be able to make this game the way that I have without what Papa taught me; I decided to make it a tribute, and to dedicate it to his memory. 

It's a simple game, just like memories it's loosely based upon. I hope it can bring you some small moments of joy and silliness and break up some of the monotony of long hours at work - at the end of the day, that's what fishin's all about.

-E

store_data.about_the_game:
THE LAST LOGIN is a narrative hacker thriller about desperation, bad choices, and the voice in your head that says it can help.

You lost your job. Rent is due. Your bank account is empty. Then the voice comes back — sharp, funny, dangerous — pushing you toward one small crime that could fix everything.

At first, it is just food. Then rent. Then bigger jobs. Then people start noticing.

Inside GHOST//OS, your in-game computer system, you will chat with dangerous contacts, inspect fake websites, use fictional terminal commands, compare intercepted responses, and make choices that quietly shape your future. Every action leaves a trace.

Key Features

  • Narrative hacker thriller set inside a dark apartment and the GHOST//OS computer system.

  • A mysterious voice in your head that guides, jokes, pressures, and tempts you.

  • Fictional hacking-inspired gameplay using fake websites, terminal commands, response comparison, logs, CCTV, and safe toy systems.

  • Story choices with hidden consequences — the game tracks how reckless you become without showing morality meters.

  • Multiple endings based on how far you go and how much heat you create.

  • Cinematic apartment events including rent pressure, police attention, strange messages, and late-night consequences.

  • Dark, grounded atmosphere focused on loneliness, pressure, crime, and survival.

This is not a real hacking simulator. All systems, tools, websites, commands, and targets are fictional and built for story gameplay.

store_data.about_the_game:
How far can you climb?

Enter the Labyrinth — a massive 100-floor dungeon filled with deadly monsters, escalating challenges, and powerful bosses guarding each layer deeper below.

Fight your way through dangerous encounters, strengthen your character over time, and push further with every run.

Skill-Based Combat

Combat is built around timing, positioning, and precision.

Dodge incoming attacks, punish enemy openings, and master increasingly dangerous encounters as you descend deeper into the Labyrinth.

Every enemy presents a different threat, and survival depends on skill as much as progression.

Persistent Character Progression

Grow stronger across every attempt.

Level skills including:

  • Vitality

  • Strength

  • Defense

  • Focus

  • Magic

  • Summoning

  • Crafting

Experiment with different builds and playstyles while permanently improving your character over time.

Even defeat pushes your progression forward.

Climb Through 100 Floors

The Labyrinth is designed around long-term progression and escalating difficulty.

  • 100 floors of dungeon progression

  • Increasingly dangerous enemies

  • New monster types as you descend

  • Unique Epic Bosses every 10 floors

  • Endless build experimentation

Each floor pushes your character further.

Epic Boss Encounters

Every 10 floors introduces a powerful new boss encounter with unique mechanics, attacks, and challenges.

Learn their patterns, adapt your strategy, and overcome increasingly difficult battles to continue deeper into the Labyrinth.

Return to Town Between Runs

After each expedition, return to town to prepare for your next attempt.

  • Craft stronger equipment

  • Improve your build

  • Prepare supplies

  • Plan your next descent

Then enter the Labyrinth again and push even deeper.

Additional Features

  • Third-person anime-inspired action RPG

  • Character creation

  • Controller support

  • Procedurally generated dungeon layouts

  • Loot and equipment progression

  • Multiple build paths and playstyles

  • Infinite Mode planned during development

  • Additional skills and content planned throughout Early Access

Early Access

The game is actively being expanded throughout Early Access with additional enemies, progression systems, skills, bosses, and long-term content updates planned over development.

store_data.about_the_game:
Two wizards enter. One leaves. The other is Uncast forever.

Uncast is a pixel art roguelite where every duel is a battle of wits, timing and magic mastery. Choose your wizard, forge your spell loadout, and face an escalating gauntlet of enemies. Until you meet a boss, that will test everything you have.

⚔️ The Duel No armies. No maps. Just you and your opponent, wands raised, spells flying. Every duel is pure 1v1 wizardr. Read your enemy, pick your moment, unleash devastation. Fire meets water. Electricity tears through dark matter. Spells clash mid-air, collide, and explode. When the smoke clears, only one wizard remains.

🔮 Build Your Loadout With over 100 spells across four elements: Fire, Water, Electricity and Dark Matter. No two runs feel the same. Choose up to 6 spells before each duel, level them up between rounds, and craft combinations that obliterate. 12 neutral spells add another layer of strategy. 24 wands change how your magic behaves. 64 upgrades reshape your stats. 32 potions give you the edge when everything is on the line.

🧙 Choose Your Wizard 12 playable wizards, each a master of their element. Each with their own identity, playstyle and wand. Find yours.

🌍 8 Worlds. 16 Bosses. Fight through 8 hand-crafted pixel art worlds. From dark desert forests to volcanic castles. Each with its own atmosphere. Every third opponent is a boss. Sixteen of them stand between you and the most powerful wand in existence. They will not go quietly.

♾️ The Roguelite Loop Die. Learn. Rebuild. Between duels, spend your earnings in the upgrade shop, sharpen your spells, and choose your next potion. Every run gives you something new to try. Every death teaches you something. The loop is deep, fast and dangerously addictive.

🌐 Challenge the World Think you've mastered the arcane arts? Prove it. Challenge a friend or face a random opponent in online PvP duels. The same spell-clashing, wand-raising intensity: Now against a real wizard, who casts to Uncast you.

store_data.about_the_game:
One village. One night. Not a single witness. And no turning back.

Danila is a folklorist historian who agreed to help his friend Roma with one "simple" job. Come to godforsaken Zmeyevka, dig up an ancient chest, and receive seven million rubles. The client didn't reveal his name or face, but he paid an advance. What difference does it make, right?

They broke the seal. They released the Morok. Now Zmeevka has come to life. The huts breathe, the fog whispers with the voices of the dead, and black threads of a curse crawl beneath their skin. The village won't let them go easily. And their own consciousness tells them: "Kill your friend. Take the chest. Only then will you survive."

GAMEPLAY

This is a psychological visual novel with an emphasis on atmosphere and moral choice. Gameplay revolves around reading dialogue, Dani's internal monologues, and making decisions in critical situations.

Each choice can:

save the hero,

destroy them,

Only text, suspense, and the feeling of being watched.

GAME FEATURES

Slavic horror. Horror is born from silence and your own thoughts, which begin to sound like someone else's.

Paranoia as a game mechanic. The Morok feeds on your fears, greed, and doubts. Do you trust your friend? Or are you ready to strike first?

Unvarnished folklore. Chernobog's rune, Mavkas, a charmed chest, a lead seal—no Hollywood hype. Just what people believed in remote villages a hundred years ago.

Multiple endings and hidden dead ends. One wrong look into the water, one step toward a voice in the fog—and you'll forever remain a part of Zmeevka.

store_data.about_the_game:
In Star Journey, you are the captain of a crewed starship caught in a war between the United Worlds and the Neo Terrans.

Travel a living starmap of claimed worlds, hostile fleets, neutral powers, spaceports, unexplored systems, and dangerous anomalies. Take command from inside your ship: pilot through space, raise shields, fire torpedoes, manage power, repair hull damage, consult your officers, and decide where your crew goes next.

The frontier is full of incidents waiting for a captain’s judgment. Rescue stranded survey teams, investigate suspicious distress beacons, uncover ancient probes, stabilize unstable anomalies, make first contact with new civilizations, and decide whether defecting enemy captains deserve asylum. Some missions lead to diplomacy. Some lead to discovery. Some are traps.

Beyond the bridge, the war continues. Factions move fleets, defend homeworlds, patrol borders, capture systems, repair damaged ships, and lose captains. Your actions leave a persistent mark: ships are damaged or destroyed, passengers come aboard, prisoners are held, discoveries are recorded, and explored systems remain explored.

Build if you want to. Fight if you must. Explore because the frontier is waiting.

Feature List

  • Choose your side in a war between the United Worlds and the Neo Terrans.

  • Command your starship from inside the ship using piloting, science, weapons, power, comms, integrity, teleporter, medical, and captain consoles.

  • Explore a persistent starmap of friendly, hostile, neutral, claimed, and unexplored systems.

  • Fight enemy ships and pirates with shields, torpedoes, hull damage, fires, explosions, and catastrophic ship destruction.

  • Land on planets, visit spaceports, shop, repair your ship, and investigate special landing sites.

  • Take on science-driven episodes including distress calls, ancient probes, unstable anomalies, stranded expeditions, first contact, and enemy captain asylum.

  • Make first contact with new people, and perhaps invite them to join your faction!

  • Manage crew morale, call officer meetings, receive reports, and hear your crew react to discoveries and decisions.

  • Rescue survivors, transport passengers, capture enemy captains, and deliver defectors to your homeworld.

  • Use autopilot and target-frame HUD labels to navigate to planets, ships, beacons, probes, anomalies, derelicts, and landing sites.

  • Mine resources from asteroids, craft items, trade goods, repair damage, and build or modify voxel starships.

  • Experience a living faction war with persistent fleets, captains, ship damage, system control, prisoners, rescues, and battlefield outcomes.

  • Save and load persistent quest progress, ship hull damage, passengers, fleet state, exploration records, and starmap changes.

Command your starship. Choose your side. Shape the frontier.

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome to the Kernel.

In RE_ALLOC, you don’t just write code; you design the architecture of execution. This is a technical simulation where assembly logic meets hardware constraints. You are tasked with constructing intrusion pipelines using a grid of CPUs, Stack RAM, and Indexed Memory nodes.

Your goal is not just to make the code run, but to make it perfect. Every cycle counts. Every instruction must be optimized. Every data flow must be calculated.

Key Features:

  • Assembly Engineering: Write raw, low-level assembly code. Master your registers, handle memory pointers, and navigate conditional jumps to solve complex logic puzzles.

  • Grid-Based Architecture: Design your own hardware topology. Map your mission data across a grid, connect ports, and define how your nodes communicate.

  • Optimization Challenges: Don't just solve it—solve it efficiently. Your performance is measured by cycle counts, node usage, and instruction density.

  • Strict Logic: There is no room for error. A memory overflow, a deadlock, or an infinite loop will crash the system. Debug your logic and test your pipeline.

  • Minimalist Aesthetic: A clean, terminal-focused interface designed for absolute focus. No hand-holding, no distractions—only you and the machine.

The Constraints: The hardware is limited. The input is fixed. The execution path is yours to define. Do you have the discipline to optimize the memory, or will your process stall under the load?

Boot the terminal. The assembly starts now.

store_data.about_the_game:
A Simulation Game About Spotting Scalpers and Running a Healthy Business

Some people buy up limited-edition products and hard-to-find popular items for their own profit, then resell them at prices far above retail.

They are known as scalpers.

In recent years, scalping has become a serious issue in the trading card game industry…

In this game, you become the owner of a card shop and aim to build a popular, well-loved store.

As the player, you will handle everything from purchasing packs and boxes to gathering information on recent card market trends through social media and video platforms. Use that knowledge to buy and sell wisely, and work your way toward becoming one of the top shops in the card game industry.

How to Play ① Information Gathering: Research the Market and Scalper Activity

Gathering information before opening the shop is an important part of running a card store.

On the video-sharing platform “WowTube,” new videos are posted every day covering recent card price trends, trending packs, must-watch cards, incidents involving scalpers, and even disputes at local shops.

Which cards should you stock?
What items are likely to spike in price?
And when a suspicious customer visits your store, what questions should you ask to expose contradictions?

Hidden within those videos are hints for increasing your sales, as well as clues for identifying scalpers.

Simply selling cards is not enough to protect your shop.
Gather information, read the mood, and predict the next wave before it hits.
Your decisions will affect both today’s sales and your shop’s reputation.

How to Play ② Purchasing Stock: Visit Wholesalers on Your Days Off

Your days off are the time to prepare for your next business day.

Visit multiple wholesalers within a limited amount of time and search for products that match the current market and your customer base. Popular cards, trending packs, hidden gems — what you choose to stock can greatly affect the following week’s sales.

However, your usual wholesalers will not always have the items you want.
If your timing is bad, your regular supplier may barely have anything in stock.

In those situations, you can visit wholesalers you do not yet have a relationship with and try to negotiate a deal. Whether they are willing to sell to an unfamiliar shop depends on them. But if you have built up a strong reputation through your daily business, new doors may begin to open.

Which wholesaler will you visit?
Which products are worth your time and money?
And when will you take a risk?

How you spend your limited days off will shape the future of your card shop.

How to Play ③ Business Days: Buy and Sell While Spotting Scalpers

On business days, you place the packs and boxes you purchased on the shelves and sell them to customers who visit your store.
At times, you may also appraise and buy cards that customers bring in.

However, not every customer is a genuine card game fan.

Some customers may be scalpers trying to buy up products for their own profit.
Pay close attention to what they are buying, what they say, and any unnatural behavior. Do not overlook even the smallest sense that something is off.

When a customer seems suspicious, you can ask them questions yourself.
Why are they buying it? Which cards are they collecting? Why do they need that many?

If their answers begin to contradict each other, you can confront them directly.

“You’re a scalper, aren’t you?”

They will not admit it easily.
Listen carefully as they try to talk their way out, expose the contradictions in their words, and uncover who they really are.

However, what you do with a customer once you know they are a scalper is up to you.
You can kick them out of the shop, or you can knowingly accept them and continue trading.

Some scalpers may have circumstances that pushed them into reselling.
Will you forgive them? Judge them? Choose profit? Or protect trust?

Your choices will greatly change both your shop’s reputation and the direction of the story.

store_data.about_the_game:
Tiny Lumi, Big Adventure

Lumibloom is a cute, cozy, colorful survivor roguelite where you play as Lumi, a tiny glowing Lumibun traveling across a magical world overcome by mysterious sleep.

Move, dash, collect XP Star Gems, and choose powerful upgrades as waves of creatures affected by magical sleep close in from every direction. With every wave, Lumi grows stronger with devastating attacks, powerful abilities, faster movement, and new ways to survive.

The First Adventure: Glowberry Grove

The current adventure begins in a magical forest grove filled with Sproutlings, Thornbugs, Bulb Brutes, Spore Floaters, and other creatures. Survive long enough and you’ll wake Nocturnip, a cranky forest boss who may not be as scary as he seems.

Choose Your Build

Level up during each run and pick from upgrade cards that change how Lumi fights. Unlock attacks, strengthen your favorite powers, improve your movement, collect gems faster, and build toward a screen full of cute chaos.

Features

  • Cute & cozy survivor roguelite / auto-attacker gameplay

  • Play as Lumi, a glowing bunny Lumibun

  • Dodge waves of creatures affected by magical sleep

  • Collect XP Star Gems and choose from powerful magical upgrade cards

  • Unlock attacks like Glow Nuzzle, Sunseed Fireball, Sparkle Zap, Tiny Black Hole, Lumi Mist, and more

  • Discover helpful pickups like Heart Jelly, Magnet Beans, Speed Sprouts, Shield Bubbles, and Bloom Chests throughout each run

  • Face Nocturnip in the first major boss fight

  • Set new local records for survival time, kills, level, and victories

  • Built for replayable runs, powerful upgrade builds, and fast-paced magical combat

A Bigger World Is Coming

Lumibloom begins in Glowberry Grove, but the world is much bigger than one forest. Future regions will take Lumi and other playable heroes beyond the grove into new locations, with their own enemies, attacks, bosses, and magical surprises.

store_data.about_the_game:
Hit the puck, drive it home.

Online 1v1 battles: smash the puck into your opponent's goal! Wield your mallet, control the puck, and clash across a fully 3D court — a new dimension of air hockey awaits.

Easy online play with keywords

Matchmaking is dead simple. Enter a keyword and you'll instantly match with another player who entered the same one. Leave it blank for a random match, or set a secret word to play with friends. No fiddly menus, no configuration.

A new dimension: depth

Regular air hockey is a flat battle. OSAKANA PING PONG isn't. The 3D court extends in every direction — line drives that punch through to the back goal, curve shots fired off lateral slides, baiting an opponent's dash and waiting to counter. Mind games stretch across every axis.

When you hit the puck with your mallet, it always heads toward the opponent's goal. The only questions are how you bend it, and how fast you send it.

Simple controls, infinite mind games

  • WASD / Arrow keys — 2D movement within your side of the court
  • Space — Dash. Bursts in the input direction; if no direction is held, charges toward the opponent
  • Esc — Surrender. Yield mid-match any time

A dash explodes at over 3x your normal speed. Charging forward doubles your hit power; sliding sideways while striking bends the puck's path. Just these few inputs spawn endless layers of reading — serves, counters, the rhythm of dashes.

Dash has another use. Spam it without a direction held and you'll push off your own back wall, surging deep into enemy territory. Strike from up close for surprise counter-attacks — but leave your goal wide open in exchange. Press the attack, or hold your ground? A single decision swings the match.

A world drawn by fish

The title text, the mallets, the puck, the court — all of it is formed by a swarm of 150 fish that gather into shape. With each scene transition the fish scatter and reassemble into something new. No textures, no filled polygons; everything is rendered as trembling line segments in a hand-drawn world. Depth fog layers in a deep-sea atmosphere on top of it all.

Zero-lag online with rollback netcode

Powered by GGRS rollback netcode — the gold standard in competitive fighting games. With just 31ms of input delay (2 frames at 64 FPS), online 1v1 feels as immediate as a local match. The matchmaking auto-expands its distance filter to pair you with nearby opponents first, and desync checks every 100 frames keep long matches rock-solid.

Every sound, from a formula

Zero recorded samples. Every sound is procedural audio synthesized from raw waveforms. The BGM playing on the title, lobby, and result screens is also algorithmically composed in real time. Lines on the screen, formulas in the air — nothing borrowed.

30 languages, connected to the world

Fully localized into all 30 Steam-supported languages: English, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified & Traditional), French, German, Spanish, Russian, Portuguese, Arabic, and more. The game switches automatically based on your Steam language. Every character is rendered with the same custom fuzzy-line style, preserving the hand-drawn feel across every script.


Built on a fast Rust engine (Bevy 0.18) for a snappy experience even on modest hardware.

store_data.about_the_game:
A RETRO-inspired 3D Action Adventure

End's Reach II is an exploration-heavy action adventure (metroidvania) set in an atmospheric and ambient science-fiction world. The game takes place in a semi-open world that both respects your time and doesn't hold your hand. Designed as a console-style experience that mirrors those found on older home consoles but with a modern visual edge.

It is best played with a controller but supports keyboard-only or M&K controls.

Lost in Space.. Again

Directly following the events of End's Reach: Urma once again finds himself trapped in a world he cannot understand, this time high atop the peaks on the mountainous planet of Enegrome. The revelations from the previous game now guide Urma's blade, no longer seeking revenge, but redemption. Despite being a direct sequel, all story elements from the first game will be covered and recapped, this is the perfect game to start with.

All New Movement & Powers!

Run, slide, roll, dash, hover, grapple, slam, and whatever else! All new movement unleashes the player's creativity and allows fast traversal all across the world. New vertical level design keeps you guessing what type of powers may come next. No more stamina to keep the player stuck in one place, go crazy!

New Dungeons, New Items, New Everything!

Not only will you collect the blueprints to unlock weapons, now each dungeon will have a key-item in the form of a gun. This takes puzzles to the 3rd dimension and lets you find more ways to interact with the world. With unique level design not every playthrough will be the exact same.

Greater Storytelling

Urma's quest for redemption will require the aid of many unique characters. Where the first game relied on the player's curiosity to tell it's story, End's Reach II has a greater world to uncover. While you can still recover data logs and research the planet, you can also now talk to many different alien species. Some of them will have missions for you, and others will offer help in exchange for goods. 

First Person & Third Person: Find Your Playstyle

Fight in third person with hack and slash combat, or pull the camera in to use one of the game's many ranged weapons. Of course some puzzles and encounters will require a mixture of both!

New Enemy Behaviour and Sneaking Mechanics

Enemies are now part of a breathing world, they have their own patrol patterns. Players can choose to avoid combat by sneaking, or take everything head on - but be careful, enemies are more potent than they used to be!

...

End's Reach and End's Reach II were solo-developed games, however they received support from the friends, family, asset store creators, and play-testers. Those people will be credited wherever possible. I cannot thank you all enough.

And last but certainly not least, there will NEVER be AI use in any of my games. 

Enjoy.

store_data.about_the_game:
About the Game

Change your life, one spray can at a time. You play as a young man who has just moved into the apartment above his grandmother's flower shop to start his professional life. Passionate about art and self-expression, you will quickly make this new neighborhood your own through your talent and creativity.

Street Art Simulator is a calm and relaxing experience, far from the stress of vandalism or police chases. No pressure here. Just you, your art, and a city eager to be beautified.

Key Features

  • Total Immersion (Zero Cluttered Menus): No abstract interfaces or text bars blocking your view. Everything happens through real, in-game objects! Your mobile phone serves as your menu to track missions, and with the press of a button, a cardboard box full of spray cans appears right in front of you to act as your color picker.

  • Dedicated Artistic Spots: The city isn't just a giant doodle pad, every artwork deserves the perfect canvas. Explore the streets to find specific, curated locations tailored for your murals or stickers. It’s up to you to find the perfect spot to beautify!

  • Creative Freedom at Your Own Pace: Bring your ideas to life on dedicated spots completely stress-free. No timers, no Game Over, just the pure joy of handling your tools and watching the neighborhood transform thanks to you.

  • A Colorful Neighborhood: Don't just be a passing artist; become a true member of the community! Meet your neighbors and lend them a hand through creative quests and missions to bring joy back to the neighborhood.

  • The Ultimate Cozy Vibe: After a painting session, head back to unwind in your apartment, enjoy the warm atmosphere above the flower shop... and spend some quality time with your cat!

Why Play This Game?

If you are looking for a zen artistic break away from punitive simulations, Street Art Simulator offers peaceful exploration and pure creation, all wrapped up in an ultra-immersive, comic-book-styled world.

store_data.about_the_game:
Your cannon isn't just a weapon - it's also how you launch into the air!

Master the art of flying by shooting in this minimalist physics-based destruction game.

Physics-based action

Levels feature objects and hazards that are physically simulated objects.  There's stuff that can get knocked over, launched from explosions, and/or destroyed.  Beware of hazards.  Blow up the barrels to win!

Physics-based controls

Your controls are also physics-based!  Firing your cannon will launch it in the opposite direction you're firing from.  You can use this to float in the air if you fire at the ground.  You can also destroy things by shooting your cannonball at them.

Minimalist experience

This is a small, simplistic game.  The basics can be learned in a very short time.

Easy to learn, not as easy to master

It's not too difficult to launch your cannon headlong into a structure.  But harder levels will require more precise control of your cannon and increased player skill.

This was created by a solo dev.  Hope you enjoy!

store_data.about_the_game:
A vampire-survivors-style roguelike. Pick a hero, pick a weapon, then survive as the screen fills with horrors that have one job: get to you

Bosses arrive every 90 seconds. The Butcher arrives every 5 minutes. Pickups drop, you level up, you pick one of three upgrades, then the screen fills again

What you do

  • Walk. Aim. Don't get touched
  • Pick upgrades each level. Stack weapons, stack passives. Find the build that survives 20 minutes
  • Run again with a different hero, different starting weapon, different seed

What's in it

  • 6 heroes, each with a different starting weapon
  • 6 weapons across 7 levels each
  • 11 passives that change how the build plays
  • Distinct pixel-art enemies, weapons and bosses
  • A procedural soundtrack that escalates with the enemy waves
  • Full gamepad support, PlayStation, Xbox and Switch glyphs all native
  • Cloud saves across machines via Steam
  • 20 achievements

What it isn't

  • A roguelite with permanent meta-progression. Every run starts fresh
  • A long game. Runs are 5 to 20 minutes

Made by

A solo dev project by Radu Ursache (RanduSoft)
Eternal Onslaught started as a browser game and grew up into the desktop release you're looking at now
Fun fact: every sprite, every sound effect, and every beat of music in the game is generated from code, no external art or audio assets.

store_data.about_the_game:
About the game Random Horse Derby is a minimalist, fully automatic, and strictly single-player horse racing game.

The concept is simple: for each race, you choose your favorite among 5 horses. The race then unfolds completely on its own before your eyes. The goal is to get as many victories as possible in order to climb the world leaderboard, thanks to a scoreboard based on your total successes.

Great for playing with friends (at home or on stream) Even though the game is purely single-player and features no virtual money system, you can easily use it to bet with friends! The main player selects their horse in the game, everyone else picks their favorite out loud, and all that's left is to watch who wins.

Features:

  • Single-player experience: You are the only one interacting with the game to choose your horse among the 5 runners.

  • Automatic races: Once the choice is made, just watch the race unfold.

  • World leaderboard: A simple leaderboard based on your total number of victories.

  • Betting with friends: Perfect for having fun betting together in front of the same screen or on stream.

store_data.about_the_game:
BlassHole is a space action, looting and survival game where you start with a modest ship and carve your way through the galaxy by raiding convoys, defeating threats and collecting whatever drifts out of the wreckage.

This is a game I made more than 25 years ago while I was studying programming. Now, finally, I have been able to remake it with everything I always imagined for it.

Explore star systems, upgrade your ship with modules, buy and sell with merchants, gather credits and parts, and decide when you are ready to jump into more dangerous territory.

Every fight can leave you with better weapons, engines, shields, hull plating or power cores. Survive long enough and your small ship can become a brutal machine.

But the galaxy does not wait: aliens, raiders, hostile stations, minibosses and final bosses guard the most valuable systems.

Features

  • OpenGL 3D space combat with cannons, missiles, auto-turrets, shields, cloak and afterburner

  • Module system with rarities, tiers and ship power management

  • Skill progression for hull, shields, weapons, engines, fuel and navigation

  • Galaxy systems with rising difficulty, merchants, special bosses and NG+ content

  • Loot credits, parts and modules to sell, equip or fold into your build

  • Ship codex and local achievement tracking prepared for future Steam integration

Gameplay Loop

  • Explore a system

  • Find targets, merchants and threats

  • Fight and collect loot

  • Sell, buy and equip new modules

  • Upgrade your ship and skills

  • Jump to a more dangerous system

Note

BlassHole is a compact space action experience built for quick runs, steady progression and getting straight back into combat.

  • Offline progress; earn while you sleep

store_data.about_the_game:
Crave the Burn


When the valley ignites and the harvest clock won't stop, every choice becomes triage—and every kiss leaves a mark.

Crave the Burn is an Adult Romance Visual Novel set in Northern California wine country during a catastrophic wildfire season—right as harvest begins and everything that matters comes due at once. You play as Garrett Mercer, the steady, weathered head winemaker of Vesper Ridge, balancing smoke-taint deadlines, evacuation orders, and the brutal math of what can be saved. Then three women arrive with three different claims on his night. With one branching choice that commits your route, romance unfolds under ash-filled skies where legacy, pride, and survival burn together.

Meet the Cast




Frankie Vega — "The Rival"
Frankie is the self-made owner-winemaker of Coyote Ridge, the scrappy upstart across the valley—and Garrett's rival of eleven years with a scoreboard she keeps out loud. When the fire runs toward her indefensible slope first, pride becomes a luxury she can't afford, and the only refuge is the one estate built to survive: his. Their relationship burns hot with competitive chemistry, grief, and the brutal vulnerability of needing the person you swore you'd beat.



Blair Holloway — "The Adjuster"
Blair is Sentinel Pacific's senior large-loss adjuster: polished, precise, and trained to deliver catastrophe in the conditional—until the road closes and the wildfire turns her from observer into participant. She came to assess whether Vesper Ridge is "defensible per the schedule," but the longer she shelters with Garrett's crew, the harder it becomes to keep calling a home an asset.



Elodie Vautrin — "The Inheritance"
Elodie is the founder's estranged daughter and sole blood heir, returning after eleven years with a Master of Wine palate, a lawyer's letter, and a grief sharpened into precision. On paper, she outranks Garrett—yet the cellar, the crew, and the ridge answer to him, and neither of them can pretend that doesn't cut. Two people circling the same dead man, deciding whether Vesper Ridge is something to claim… or something to choose.

Key Features


  • Single-choice route structure with high-stakes commitment: One decisive early choice locks in a complete romance arc—no filler, no waffling, just consequence.
  • A wildfire thriller backdrop with real procedural tension: Evacuation timelines, road closures, private vs. public fire defense, and "defensible space" triage shape every scene.
  • Three distinct romance fantasies rooted in conflict: Inheritance (the returning heir), Rivalry (the enemy forced into alliance), and Complicity (the professional who becomes personal).
  • A grounded, sensory setting—wine craft under pressure: Harvest decisions, cellar work, and smoke risk aren't window dressing—they're the language of intimacy and survival.
  • Themes with teeth: Who gets defended and who gets released? What do you stand in the smoke for when you can't save everything?
  • Adult content: Each romance route includes explicit adult scenes.

store_data.about_the_game:
Space Nomads is an open-ended space RPG where you begin with little more than a ship, a crew and a shared ambition. Explore star systems, hire crew members, trade, fight, complete contracts, and create your own path across a living galaxy. Become a trader, bounty hunter, explorer, salvager, mercenary, or something in between.

NPCs have their own tasks, whether it be mining the nearest asteroid cluster, patrolling the system, or fighting each other. Events will randomly take place in Space Nomads, such as dogfights, it's your decision to get involved or not.

The galaxy of Space Nomads is procedurally generated, everything from the galaxy itself, to the ships. The procedural generation doesn't tell you how to play, it builds the universe and leaves the choices to you.

You choose who you fly with. Crew have personality traits and provide buffs for your ship. You can find crew in space stations or escape pods. Crew write in their journal, responding to events in the world. Perhaps you targeted an innocent civilian ship? Your crew might have something to say about that.

You choose what kind of ship you want. Find components and build a sleek fighter, or... Build something that looks like it's about to fall apart. Attach weapons, utility devices and decide what your ship is capable of. 

Want to become a miner? Trader? Or just a menace to the galaxy? You decide how to create your fortune and reputation.

store_data.about_the_game:
Conquer the Woodland. Outsmart Your Rivals.

Command adorable woodland factions in a strategic battle for territory where every decision matters — because everyone moves at once.

Fight for control across a charming grid-based world of forests, rivers, and contested lands populated by animal warriors. Expand your territory, predict enemy plans, and let fate decide the battlefield through simulated dice-driven combat.

But this isn't a traditional turn-based strategy game.

Every player locks in their orders simultaneously. Attack, reinforce, expand, or bluff — then watch the entire turn unfold all at once in a chaotic clash of strategy, prediction, and calculated risk.

Victory belongs to the clever, not just the strongest. 

Gameplay

Play against other players, fill empty slots with bots, or mix both for the perfect battle.

Create and join lobbies with up to 8 players and customize each match with a wide range of optional rules, including Keeps, Attack and Defense modifiers, Fog of War, and many more.

Battles take place in simultaneous turns, allowing all players to act at the same time without waiting for opponents. Each turn begins with a recruitment phase, where players choose territories to recruit new troops and perform a single reinforcement action to move troops between connected territories.

Once all recruitment plans are locked in, they are revealed simultaneously. Players then plan their attacks, launching as many offensives as their available troops allow. When everyone is ready, all battle plans are revealed and resolved together.

Expand your territory, strengthen your armies, and outmaneuver your rivals until victory is yours.

Win by eliminating all other players, controlling every Keep on the map, or holding the Throne for three consecutive turns.

Features

Simultaneous Turn Strategy
No waiting for opponents. Every player acts at the same time, creating fast-paced tactical gameplay built around prediction and mind games.

🎲 Dice-Based Territory Battles
Conquer enemy land through simulated dice combat where preparation, positioning, and probability matter as much as luck.

Grid-Based Tactical Warfare
Expand your borders, defend critical territory, and control the map to outmaneuver rival woodland factions.

Charming Woodland World
Lead adorable chibi-inspired animal civilizations through a colorful cartoon forest setting filled with personality.

Outplay Your Opponents
Anticipate enemy movements, set traps, and exploit openings as simultaneous actions create unexpected battlefield moments.

🌲 Easy to Learn, Hard to Master
Simple territory conquest mechanics combine with deep strategic possibilities for endlessly replayable matches.

Can you predict your rivals… before they make their move?

Claim the woodland.

store_data.about_the_game:
Catch the cats at all costs! Or... press the button and blow everything up?!

"Cat Or Explosion" is a single-screen, room-clearing point-and-click game where you try to catch adorable cats.

■ Two Ways to Clear Every Room

Every single room comes equipped with a "Cat" and an "Explosion Button"!

Will you catch the cat like a civilized person, give up and press the button, or... just press it anyway because you want to??

The choice is entirely yours! In some rooms, pressing the button might actually be the harder challenge?!

Can you clear every room using both methods?

■ 50 Stages Packed with Gimmicks!

Every room features different and unique Gimmicks!

Use your wits to catch these free-spirited cats!

(※ There is a possibility of more rooms being added via future updates or DLC.)

■ No Language Barrier! Intuitive Fun for Everyone

There is absolutely no text reading or math required to play.

While the supported languages are English and Japanese, text is only used for the user interface (menus, etc.) and will not affect your ability to enjoy the actual game.

■ Play Your Way! Full Input Support

Playable with just a mouse! Just a keyboard! Or just a controller!

No configuration needed—enjoy the exact same smooth controls on whichever device you prefer.

■ More Rooms Added Based on Sales!

We plan to add brand-new rooms through updates based on total copies sold!

Enjoy the game and look forward to more content!

Next Goal: 100 copies sold → 10 New Rooms!

──────────────────────────────────

※ Cat Or Explosion is a complete remake of the original web game of the same name. We have completely overhauled the system, redesigned all existing stages, and added plenty of brand-new rooms.

Video Posting and Live Streaming Guidelines

You are fully permitted to post videos and live stream this game, including the ending. Monetization using the official features provided by streaming platforms (such as ads, Super Chats, etc.) is completely fine. For more details, please refer to our official webpage.
